NASA predicts signs of alien life will be found by 2025. What would happen to us, society, science if this turns out to be true?

To be honest, I wont be that shocked because chances are good it wont be intelligent life. I am sure they will find something, a micro-organism, maybe some fungus, or even more excitingly a worm of some sort.

The odds of finding an alien species that is as intelligent as us would be very low.

However, to go along with your discussion, what if we did meet an intelligent species of Alien. My question to you would be if they would view us as intelligent? You know how we are always thumbing our noses at monkeys and laughing at their use of primitive tools and hand gestures? What if the aliens we meet view us in the same way with our limited technology, our in fighting among members of our own species and inability to explore vast regions of space?

I don't even think it'd need to be an intelligent species to be world changing. It would be a first if it's confirmed. Life exists outside of the Earth.

Even if that life is microbial, it still means a lot of shifting in world views. I mean - is that covered in any major religions? If so, how? Would there be a sudden shift when it dawns on the public that we aren't as unique in the Universe as we thought we were? Or would it be just another science news story that was forgotten in short order?

I see where you are going with this now.

I think it would have a profound effect on many people but realistically I don't see at least my generation being that shocked by it. If I were to hear this news today and it was confirmed it would just confirm everything I have thought from the beginning. I would hope that more support would be gathered for exploratory science in space in order to further our understanding of alien species and to see if maybe there is even a shared Genome within creatures of our universe. That would be amazing to discover. Just imagine the possibility that all life is related or comes from a related source?

However the older generations, the generations that are rooted in deep religious faiths and stern world views, this could shock them quite badly... or they will get a dose of Fox News and just pretend its all a hoax. For some reason older generations are very good with denial.

I don't know if people would actually change at all or have any sort of epiphanies. We live on a planet full of life, some of that life shows clear signs of sentience, of thoughts and emotions, of being people in their own way, just like us. That doesn't stop humans from believing that we are god's special chosen animals, that we aren't even animals, that everything else that exists is just a prop or a tool or a toy. I think that unless the life we discover is humanoid and has some form of language, it will be insignificant to most people. The religious minded will say that god is great and works mysteriously, the business minded will calculate how much money can be made from it and collectively we will dream of one day mining and plundering alien planets while we continue to righteously destroy our own and everything that lives on it.

Edit: I just want to add that if we did discover 'intelligent' life and it was peaceful or primitive, I imagine we would see a rerun of the native American Indian or the Australian Aborigine or the Southern African Bushman. Some humans may be intelligent but I believe the majority of us are violent, psychotic idiots and I don't think we're ready to discover any other intelligent life. I just hope it would be ready for us.

I've heard my uber-religious mother already mention the idea of life-seeding, as an explanation for how God's creation could establish itself on an extraterrestrial body. I have complete faith in the orthodoxies' ability to use pseudo-science to perpetuate mythology.

I agree with v/WowAFreeBeer that it is unlikely we will find anything very advanced. However, finding any life will have some impact on how humans see themselves, especially in the realms of religion and ecology.

Monotheist religions will have to make room in their cosmology for other life forms. I know several Sci-Fi authors have dealt with this problem.

Ecologically, we will all have to consider what life really is, and how we damage/encourage it on our own world. Can we learn from our world and apply that knowledge to make wise decisions about how to treat extra-terrestrial life? Can we make money from it?

I think there would be a couple big changes in our world's world view, but the really cool changes would be small and slow.
